part.text:
Fixed. The issue was that localized integer formatting ignored the presentation type: `loc_writer` always wrote decimal digits, and the grouping-aware `write_int` only supported base 10 with a single-char (sign) prefix.

Changes in `include/fmt/format.h`:
- **`write_int` with `digit_grouping`** (include/fmt/format.h:2122) now supports all integer presentation types (`d`, `x`/`X`, `b`/`B`, `o`) by generating digits in the requested base and applying locale grouping to them.
- **Prefix encoding/decoding** in that function now handles multi-character prefixes (`-`, `0x`, `0X`, `0b`, `0`) via the existing `prefix_append` size-in-bits encoding instead of assuming one char.
- **`loc_writer::operator()`** (include/fmt/format.h:2500) now applies alternate-form prefixes (`#`) per type and falls back to the standard (non-locale) path for `c` (`chr`) so it formats a character correctly.

Verified:
- `fmt::format(loc, "{:LX}", 123456789)` → `7,5BC,D15`; `{:Lx}` → `7,5bc,d15`; `{:#Lb}` → `-0b111,010,110,...`; `{:10Lo}` → `"    30,071"`; `{:L}`/`{:Ld}` grouping, float localization, `{:Lc}`, and `{:LX}` under the C locale all behave correctly (matching the new `format_test.format_locale` cases).
- Full test suite passes: 20/20 in ctest (format, xchar, chrono, etc.), plus a header-only (`FMT_HEADER_ONLY`) build sanity check including `fmt::group_digits`.
